transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I'm here because... well, it's been nearly two years now, and I just know the contractor and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. And it doesn't matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give, I know what's going on. It’s just like that time we tried to get the landscaping done back in '98, you know? We hired this fellow, seemed nice enough, drove a blue truck... or was it green? No, it was definitely blue because it matched the neighbor's mailbox, the one who moved away to Florida. Anyway, he promised he’d plant these beautiful azaleas, but instead, he put in rhododendrons. Can you imagine? Rhododendrons! And they need completely different soil, which I told him, but nobody listens to a woman my age. Just like now with the kitchen. They think I don't see them whispering when they think I'm not looking.
Do you think these people are working against you specifically, or is it more about the project in general?

Oh, it is absolutely against us. Like I was saying, for nearly two years now, I’ve been completely sure that the contractor and those people on my block are quietly working together to cheat us. They are keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose! And it doesn't matter how many receipts my husband shows me to try and prove they're buying the right materials. 

He keeps all those receipts in this old shoebox... a New Balance box, actually. He started wearing those chunky white sneakers a few years ago because his arches were falling. The foot doctor told him—Dr. Miller, over by the old Sears that closed down, you know the one? They turned it into a spirit Halloween store last October. Anyway, Dr. Miller told Frank he needed more support if he was going to keep bowling on Thursdays. Frank just loves his bowling league. They have matching shirts and everything, though the yellow really washes him out. 

But anyway, Frank pulls out these receipts from the box, and the contractor gives us all these excuses about measurements and backorders, but I know the truth. I know they are doing it to us on purpose.
Do you think anyone else shares your belief that the contractor and your neighbors are working against you?

Well, no, I don't think so. Frank certainly doesn't, he just keeps showing me those receipts. And my daughter, Susan, well, she lives all the way out in Seattle now, so she isn't around to see it. 

Seattle... you know, it rains so much out there. I went to visit her back in 2015. Or maybe it was 2016? I remember we went to that big market where the men throw the fish around. Pike Place, they call it. The smell was just awful, honestly. I really don't know how people can eat seafood that's just been sitting out on ice all day like that. It reminds me of the time I got terrible food poisoning from a tuna salad sandwich at the church summer picnic. Pastor Dave made it, and he used that cheap mayonnaise. You know the kind, the store brand with the flimsy yellow label? I told him right then, I said, 'Dave, you really can't skimp on mayonnaise when it's sitting out in the sun,' but he never listens. Nobody really listens to me, to be honest. 

So... no, I suppose no one else really sees what they're doing to my kitchen.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't think the contractor and your neighbors were working against you?

Well, I mean, before they started the work, everything was perfectly fine. It’s really been going on for about a year and nine months now. That’s exactly when the kitchen and the garden remodeling started and just completely disrupted the whole house. 

The garden was supposed to be the easy part, really. I just wanted some nice raised beds for my tomatoes. I always try to grow the Big Boy tomatoes, you know? Well, I used to, anyway, back when we lived over on Elm Street in the eighties. We had this wonderful soil there, just so dark and rich. My neighbor there, Mrs. Higgins, she used to bake the most incredible zucchini bread from her garden and she'd bring a loaf over every Tuesday. She always wrapped it in that nice wax paper with a little red ribbon. I asked for her recipe once, and she told me it was a strict family secret. But between you and me, doctor, I saw her buying the Betty Crocker mix at the Piggly Wiggly! I never said a word to her about it, though, I just smiled and thanked her. People can be so funny about their pride, can't they? 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the contractor. So, no, before a year and nine months ago, I didn't think they were doing anything to me. But once the house got torn up and the disruption started, it all became very obvious what they were up to.
Have you ever had a time since the remodeling started where you doubted that the contractor and your neighbors were working against you?

Doubted it? No, not for a single minute. Like I was telling you earlier, it's been nearly two years now, and I am just as sure today as I was then that the contractor and those neighbors are quietly working together to cheat us. They are keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and no amount of Frank waving those receipts in my face or the contractor giving me his silly excuses is going to make me doubt what I can see with my own two eyes. 

I mean, you just have to look at the backsplash to know I'm right. They used the completely wrong grout color! I specifically picked out "Alabaster," but what they put up is clearly "Antique White." White is such a tricky color to get right, really. I remember when I painted my first apartment white back in 1976. Well, the landlord painted it, I suppose. He was a funny little man, Mr. Abernathy. He always wore these thick suspenders with little trout embroidered on them. He just loved fly fishing. He went up to Maine every single summer for it, rain or shine. 

I've never been to Maine myself, but I hear the lobster rolls up there are just to die for. Though, like I said about that church picnic, after my incident with Pastor Dave's tuna salad, I am very, very careful about any kind of seafood mixed with mayonnaise. You really have to keep it chilled on ice, and you can't just leave it sitting out on a picnic table under an oak tree. The squirrels were even staying away from it by the end of the afternoon! 

But yes, to answer your question... no, I haven't had any doubts at all. I know exactly what they're doing to my kitchen.
Have you ever had a day where you didn't think the contractor and your neighbors were working against you since the remodeling started?

I feel like we're going in circles, doctor! Like I just said a moment ago, no, not for a single day. I'm here because for nearly two years now, I've been absolutely sure that the contractor and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us. They want to keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and it doesn't matter how many receipts my husband Frank shows me, or how many excuses they give me. I know what I know. 

Speaking of Frank's receipts, he saves every single piece of paper, you know. He keeps them all in this old shoebox in the den. It’s a Buster Brown shoebox from... oh, it must be the early nineties. Do they even make Buster Brown shoes anymore? I remember buying a pair for my Susan when she was starting first grade. We went to the indoor mall, the one that used to have that big beautiful fountain right in the center where people threw pennies and made wishes. I always told Susan not to touch the water, though, because you just don't know where those pennies have been. People keep change in their pockets with lint and dirty tissues and goodness knows what else. 

My Uncle Arthur used to keep butterscotch candies in his pocket right alongside his loose change. He'd offer you a candy, and it would always have little bits of pocket fuzz stuck to the wrapper. You had to peel it off so carefully! He was a sweet man, though. He worked at the post office down on Main Street for forty years, back when stamps only cost a few cents. 

But anyway... no. Not one day has gone by where I didn't know exactly what they were doing to my house.
Have you ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you questioned whether the contractor and your neighbors were really working against you?

Doctor, I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing over and over again! No, not for a moment. Not even for a second. Like I said, I'm here because for nearly two years now I've been completely sure that the contractor and some of the people on my block are quietly working together to cheat us. They want to keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. And like I told you, it doesn't matter how many receipts Frank waves around or what silly excuses they try to feed me. 

Frank has always been like that, though, believing any piece of paper someone hands him. He’s very trusting. Too trusting, if you ask me. I remember when he bought that used station wagon back in '84. The salesman handed him this handwritten paper saying the transmission was brand new, and Frank just smiled and shook his hand. Well, wouldn't you know, it broke down on our way to Mount Rushmore! 

Oh, Mount Rushmore was beautiful, though. We stopped at this little diner in South Dakota, and they had the best cherry pie I’ve ever tasted. The waitress there, she had this big hair, you know, teased up high like they used to do, and she called everyone "hon." She reminded me of my cousin Linda. Linda was a hairdresser down in Florida, Fort Lauderdale, I think. She used to send us oranges every Christmas in these big wooden crates. The crates were so sturdy, Frank used to keep his tools in them in the garage. 

But no, I've never questioned it. Not once. I know exactly what they're doing with my kitchen.
Has your belief that the contractor and neighbors are working against you ever changed in intensity?

Well, no, it hasn't changed. Not the intensity, not the feeling, nothing. I don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you, doctor. For almost two years, it's been the exact same thing—I am absolutely sure that this contractor and those neighbors of mine are in cahoots, quietly working together to cheat us and leave my kitchen half-finished and half-wrong. And it doesn't matter how many times Frank pulls out those receipts, or what kind of ridiculous excuses they come up with. The truth doesn't just change its intensity! 

Speaking of intensity, though, you should have seen the sun beating down on my hydrangeas last August. Just brutal. I had to go out there twice a day with the watering can just to keep them from crisping up like bacon. Frank bought me this lovely copper watering can for our anniversary a few years back. He found it at this little antique shop off Highway 9. The woman who ran the shop had three basset hounds just sleeping right there on the floor. You had to step right over them to look at the shelves! They had ears that practically dragged on the ground. 

My neighbor growing up, Mrs. Gable, she had a basset hound named Barnaby. He used to howl every time the fire siren went off at the station downtown. It was the saddest sound, really, like he was singing along but didn't know the words. Mrs. Gable used to give us homemade popcorn balls on Halloween instead of candy. They were always so sticky, you'd be picking caramel out of your teeth until Thanksgiving! 

But no, to answer your question... my belief hasn't changed one bit. I know exactly what they're doing.
Has anything specific happened that made you first think the contractor and your neighbors were working against you?

Well, I don't know if there was one specific thing that just popped up out of nowhere. It wasn't like a movie where someone drops a secret file or something, you know? It just... it all started when they were tearing up the old flooring. 

We had this lovely pale yellow linoleum in there for years. Frank always said it looked dated, but I thought it was so bright and cheerful, especially in the mornings when the sun hit it. It reminded me of my grandmother's kitchen back in Ohio. Oh, she had the most wonderful kitchen! She used to bake these incredible lemon meringue pies on Sundays. The meringue was always so tall and fluffy, just like big clouds. She swore the secret was using room-temperature egg whites and a real copper bowl. I tried making it once for the church bake sale back in, oh, it must have been '98, but my meringue completely collapsed on the drive over. It looked so sad sitting there on the folding table next to all the perfect brownies. Pastor Miller bought a slice anyway and told me it was the best he'd ever had. He was always so polite like that. He had this booming voice, used to sing bass in the choir, and he drove this enormous baby blue Cadillac that took up two parking spaces... 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, there wasn't one big event that made me realize it. It's just the reality of the situation. I just know what I know, and I know they're working together to ruin my kitchen.
How long have you believed the contractor and your neighbors are working against you?

Well, like I've been trying to tell you, it's been going on for about a year and nine months now. It all started when the kitchen and the garden remodeling began and just completely threw the whole house into chaos. You know how it is when you have workers in your home, there's just dust absolutely everywhere. 

I was finding dust on my good china in the dining room, and that's two rooms over! My mother gave me that china when Frank and I got married. It's the Royal Albert pattern, the one with the little pink roses and the gold trim. She bought it piece by piece from a department store downtown that isn't even there anymore. They tore it down to build a parking garage, which is just a shame. The department store had an elevator with an actual operator, a nice young man in a uniform who would announce the floors. "Third floor, ladies' apparel and linens!" he'd say. You just don't see that kind of service anymore. Now everywhere you go, it's all self-checkout and machines yelling at you to place your item in the bagging area. 

I tried using one of those machines at the grocery store last Tuesday because I just needed a quick carton of milk for my tea. I drink Earl Grey in the afternoons, it settles my stomach. But the machine wouldn't scan it, and the light started flashing red, and everyone was looking at me like I was a criminal! The young girl working there had to come over and type in a code... 

But yes, a year and nine months. Ever since they started tearing everything up.
Is there anything that could happen or anything someone could show you that would make you question your belief about the contractor and your neighbors?

Well, no, absolutely not. What could they possibly show me? Frank is always waving those receipts in my face, trying to prove they bought this material or paid for that labor, but paper can be faked, doctor. It's been nearly two years now of this nonsense, and I am absolutely certain they are quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. They can give me all the excuses in the world, but it doesn't change what I know. 

Speaking of paper, though, you wouldn't believe the amount of junk mail we get lately. It's just stacks and stacks of catalogs for things I'd never buy. Yesterday I got one just for birdhouses. Who needs a catalog entirely dedicated to birdhouses? Although, I will say, they had a lovely little blue one shaped like a Victorian cottage. It reminded me of a house down the street from where we lived when I was a little girl. The Johnsons lived there, and Mrs. Johnson used to paint her front door a different color every spring. One year it was a bright, shocking pink! The neighborhood association threw an absolute fit about it. They had special meetings and everything. Mr. Henderson, who lived next door to them, he was the president of the association, and he used to patrol the sidewalks with a little notepad, writing down every infraction. He gave my father a warning once because our grass was a quarter-inch too long. A quarter-inch! Can you imagine? My father was so mad he went out and mowed the lawn at six in the morning on a Sunday just to spite him. The noise woke up half the block... 

But to answer your question, no. There is nothing anyone could show me. I know exactly what that contractor and those neighbors are up to, and no fake receipt is going to convince me otherwise.

It reminded me of my grandmother's kitchen back in Ohio. Oh, she had the most wonderful kitchen! She used to bake these incredible lemon meringue pies on Sundays. The meringue was always so tall and fluffy, just like big clouds. She swore the secret was using room-temperature egg whites and a real copper bowl. I tried making it once for the church bake sale back in, oh, it must have been '98, but my meringue completely collapsed on the drive over. It looked so sad sitting there on the folding table next to all the perfect brownies. Pastor Miller bought a slice anyway and told me it was the best he'd ever had. He was always so polite like that. He had this booming voice, used to sing bass in the choir, and he drove this enormous baby blue Cadillac that took up two parking spaces... 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, there wasn't one big event that made me realize it. It's just the reality of the situation. I just know what I know, and I know they're working together to ruin my kitchen.

doctor.question: How long have you believed the contractor and your neighbors are working against you?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about 1 year and 9 months, since the kitchen and garden remodeling started disrupting the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question "How long have you believed the contractor and your neighbors are working against you?" is directly asking about the duration of the delusion.

patient.answer:
Well, like I've been trying to tell you, it's been going on for about a year and nine months now. It all started when the kitchen and the garden remodeling began and just completely threw the whole house into chaos. You know how it is when you have workers in your home, there's just dust absolutely everywhere. 

I was finding dust on my good china in the dining room, and that's two rooms over! My mother gave me that china when Frank and I got married. It's the Royal Albert pattern, the one with the little pink roses and the gold trim. She bought it piece by piece from a department store downtown that isn't even there anymore. They tore it down to build a parking garage, which is just a shame. The department store had an elevator with an actual operator, a nice young man in a uniform who would announce the floors. "Third floor, ladies' apparel and linens!" he'd say. You just don't see that kind of service anymore. Now everywhere you go, it's all self-checkout and machines yelling at you to place your item in the bagging area. 

I tried using one of those machines at the grocery store last Tuesday because I just needed a quick carton of milk for my tea. I drink Earl Grey in the afternoons, it settles my stomach. But the machine wouldn't scan it, and the light started flashing red, and everyone was looking at me like I was a criminal! The young girl working there had to come over and type in a code... 

But yes, a year and nine months. Ever since they started tearing everything up.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's beliefs are fixed or open to change
doctor.question: Is there anything that could happen or anything someone could show you that would make you question your belief about the contractor and your neighbors?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if anything could happen or be shown to the patient that would make them question their belief, which directly relates to the fixed nature of delusions despite contradictory evidence (S019).

patient.answer:
Well, no, absolutely not. What could they possibly show me? Frank is always waving those receipts in my face, trying to prove they bought this material or paid for that labor, but paper can be faked, doctor. It's been nearly two years now of this nonsense, and I am absolutely certain they are quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. They can give me all the excuses in the world, but it doesn't change what I know. 

Speaking of paper, though, you wouldn't believe the amount of junk mail we get lately. It's just stacks and stacks of catalogs for things I'd never buy. Yesterday I got one just for birdhouses. Who needs a catalog entirely dedicated to birdhouses? Although, I will say, they had a lovely little blue one shaped like a Victorian cottage. It reminded me of a house down the street from where we lived when I was a little girl. The Johnsons lived there, and Mrs. Johnson used to paint her front door a different color every spring. One year it was a bright, shocking pink! The neighborhood association threw an absolute fit about it. They had special meetings and everything. Mr. Henderson, who lived next door to them, he was the president of the association, and he used to patrol the sidewalks with a little notepad, writing down every infraction. He gave my father a warning once because our grass was a quarter-inch too long. A quarter-inch! Can you imagine? My father was so mad he went out and mowed the lawn at six in the morning on a Sunday just to spite him. The noise woke up half the block... 

But to answer your question, no. There is nothing anyone could show me. I know exactly what that contractor and those neighbors are up to, and no fake receipt is going to convince me otherwise.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a persistent delusion of persecution, believing that the contractor and neighbors are working together to cheat them, which has been present for nearly two years. This delusion is not part of a broader psychotic disorder and is not attributable to another mental disorder or medical condition.
